newsitem.title: GERMANY: BMW shares surge on 1996 sales results.
newsitem.headline: BMW shares surge on 1996 sales results.

text.p: Shares in BMW AG surged after the German carmaker said on Thursday that its 1996 group deliveries rose seven percent to 1.15 million units and would launch at least two new products a year in the coming years.

BMW shares were up 37 marks ($22.55) in bourse trade at 1,067 marks, gaining about 20 marks after the results were released. The overall DAX-30 index was up 21.93 points, or 0.73 percent, at 3,021.13 points.
"People had generally expected worse results but the trading volumes in BMW right now at not very high," said one Frankfurt share trader.
Traders also said the BMW gains came after the shares had consolidated in recent days following a bout of profit-taking.
"Since the start of 1997, the favourable sales developments have continued," BMW said in a statement.

The car maker also reported that group sales in 1996 surged 13.3 percent to 52.27 billion marks, largley thanks to strong demand for its latest executive class 5-series model. Car production climbed 4.1 percent to 1.14 million units.
The sales and production figures marked the third straight yearly increase after BMW and the rest of the German car industry suffered from a difficult global car market in 1993.
The company did not report profit figures. In 1995, net income declined slightly to 692 million marks from 697 million marks in 1994.
BMW said it would not show off the planned new models any time soon. "We will remain true to our policy of presenting new products to the public only when they start production."
